body.name: cross-fitted bands and separated-model decisions
body.construction: Write \(t_n=\log(M_d/\alpha)/n\), and split \(\mathcal Z_n\) into regression and evaluation folds. The generic branch estimates each \(\mu_{v,A}\) off-fold by clipped least squares over degree-two local polynomials in all coordinates of \(V_A\), with bandwidth \(h_{v,A}=\min\{1,t_n^{1/(|A|+6)}\}\) when \(A\ne\varnothing\), using the constant fit when \(A=\varnothing\). Separately, the pairing-agnostic matching-adaptive branch estimates \(\mu_{v,A}\) by clipped least squares over the union of the constant sieve and, for every \(u\in A\), the univariate degree-two local-polynomial sieve in \(V_u\) with bandwidth \(h_{\mathrm{pair}}=\min\{1,t_n^{1/7}\}\); the minimizing coordinate is selected from the data and no pairing is supplied to the fit. For either branch, evaluate squared loss and bounded-kernel HSIC on held-out folds to form simultaneous intervals \(\mathcal B^R_{v,A}\) and \(\mathcal B^H_{v,A,u}\), with the branch-specific largest half-widths denoted by \(w_R\) and \(w_H\). Intersect each HSIC interval with \(\{0\}\cup[\lambda,\infty)\), recording \(\mathrm{ind}\) when the intersection contains \(0\), \(\mathrm{dep}\) when it meets \([\lambda,\infty)\), both when both are possible, and both when the intersection is empty. Propagate the risk intervals and these decisions through every insertion gain and pruning step; let \(w_S\) be the largest resulting gain half-width and let \(\widehat{\mathcal G}_n\) be the union of all compatible terminal DAGs, with all labelled DAGs returned if that union is empty. The generic and matching-adaptive branches are propagated separately.
